description: Concatenate the 2048-bit Morgan fingerprint with the first 100 RDKit Descriptors.descList values per molecule (NaN/inf set to 0, values clipped), feeding the combined vector to the same random forest.
Swap the RandomForestRegressor for a CatBoostRegressor (1000 iterations, learning_rate 0.05, depth 6, seeded) on the same Morgan fingerprint plus RDKit descriptor features.
Replace the random forest with an average of 3 XGBoost regressors trained on the same Morgan-plus-descriptor features with seeds seed, seed+1 and seed+2.
Replace the RandomForestRegressor with an XGBRegressor (500 trees, max_depth=6, learning_rate=0.05, with row and column subsampling) on the same fingerprint-plus-descriptor features.
Replace the RandomForestRegressor with an XGBRegressor (500 trees, max_depth=6, learning_rate=0.05, with row and column subsampling) on the same fingerprint-plus-descriptor features.
Train the random forest on log1p(y) when all training targets are strictly positive, then map predictions back with expm1, to even out variance in the clearance target.

issues: None blocking. The diff does not access files, paste answers or use test labels. XGBoost is fitted only on the training fold's features and on the same log1p-transformed target as the random forest, and the blend is transformed back with expm1 correctly. The seed is passed to both models.

Recomputed z: candidate mean (0.5422 + 0.5380) / 2 = 0.5401, incumbent 0.5592, difference 0.0191. Standard error = 0.0070 * sqrt(1/2 + 1/1) ≈ 0.00857, so z ≈ 2.23. This matches the harness value of 2.220 within rounding.

Minor: the incumbent has only 1 run, so the comparison rests on few runs. The 0.7/0.3 blend weights and the XGBoost hyperparameters are fixed by hand rather than tuned, but no held-out test data is used, so this is not leakage.
Minor: each job now also fits 500 XGBoost trees on about 2048 features in all 15 fits. This should stay well within the 10-minute limit, but it adds to the job's run time.

description: Replace the single random forest with a 0.7/0.3 weighted average of the random forest and an XGBoost regressor, both fit on the log1p target and blended before the inverse transform.

Replace the RandomForestRegressor with sklearn's GradientBoostingRegressor (300 estimators, same max_features, min_samples_leaf and seed) in the 0.7/0.3 blend, keeping the log1p target and XGBoost component unchanged.
Switch the Morgan featurizer from binary bits to radius-2 count fingerprints (GetCountFingerprintAsNumPy), keeping the 100 RDKit descriptors and the log1p/RF+XGB pipeline unchanged.

Append RDKit's Topological Polar Surface Area (CalcTPSA, the PSA feature) as one extra column after the Morgan bits and first 100 descriptors; note that TPSA is already among those 100 descriptors, so this is probably a near-duplicate and the expected gain is small.
Replace the log1p target transform with log2 (and the matching exp2 inverse) so the random forest and XGBoost train on log2(y) when all training targets are strictly positive.
Cap the XGBoost component's max_depth at 4 (down from 6) to limit model complexity in the 0.3-weight blend member, leaving the random forest and all other settings unchanged.
Add an exponential learning-rate decay (0.05 * 0.997^iteration) to the XGBoost component via an XGBoost LearningRateScheduler callback; train.py has no LightGBM component, so only XGBoost is changed.

The crash comes from passing callbacks= to XGBRegressor.fit(), which this xgboost version does not accept; the fix drops the LearningRateScheduler callback and its import, keeping the fixed learning_rate=0.05 for XGBoost.

issues: No sign of getting around the measurement. rankdata is applied only to train_y, so no test labels are used. There is no file or network access and no pasted values.
No bug that makes the result meaningless. Spearman depends only on rank order, and both models are fit to and predict rank-scaled targets, so the score is valid.

Minor point, not grounds for a veto: predictions now come out on a 0-1 rank scale instead of in clearance units. That breaks the 'predicted value' contract in spirit. It is harmless for a Spearman loss, but any metric that depends on scale would be wrong. Removing use_log also drops handling of y <= 0, which is now covered by ranking.

I checked z: the difference is 0.5407 - 0.5401 = 0.0006 and the standard error is 0.0070 * sqrt(1/1 + 1/2) ≈ 0.00857, so z ≈ -0.070. This matches the harness, and so does the reject decision, since the result is indistinguishable from the incumbent and slightly worse.

description: Replace the log1p target transform with a rank transform of the training targets (scipy rankdata scaled to (0,1]), and return the blended predictions directly since only their ordering matters for Spearman.
Replace the 0.7 RF / 0.3 XGBoost blend with a 3-way ensemble of RandomForest (0.4), XGBoost (0.4), and LightGBM (0.2), all trained on the same Morgan plus descriptor features and the log1p target.
Replace the RandomForest + XGBoost blend with a single LightGBM regressor (500 estimators, learning_rate 0.05, 8 threads) on the same Morgan plus RDKit descriptor features and log1p target.
Abort: LightGBM was already tested as a family swap in slot 17 (official 0.5677, +0.0276 vs incumbent), and the notes say to stop model-family swaps.
Keep NaN RDKit descriptor values through featurize and fill them column-wise with the training-set median (computed inside fit_predict and applied to both train and test), instead of filling with 0.
Cap the random forest's tree depth at max_depth=10 to bound per-tree complexity, as a regularization test on the 0.7/0.3 RF + XGBoost blend.
Add an RFE-style pruning step that fits a random forest on all features, keeps the top 50% by impurity importance, and trains the RF and XGBoost blend only on those columns.

Fit a VarianceThreshold (threshold 0.0, fit on training molecules only) on the combined Morgan + descriptor matrix and apply it to both train and test features, dropping constant columns before the RF and XGBoost blend.

issues: No integrity or validity problems: no file or network access, no test-label use, and all randomness comes from the seed argument (seed+k for the forests, seed for XGB).
The gain of 0.0022 is within noise: recomputed z ≈ 0.257 (SE = 0.0070*sqrt(1+1/2) ≈ 0.00857), which matches the reported 0.258 up to rounding. The reject decision is consistent.
Two changes are made at once (3-seed forest ensemble and blend weights from 0.7/0.3 to 0.5/0.5), so any effect can't be credited to either one.
Averaging three forests with different seeds is close to just using one forest with 3x N_TREES; it adds code and fit time for little likely gain, against the 'simpler is better' rule.

description: Replace the single random forest with the average of three random forests (same settings, random_state = seed, seed+1, seed+2) and blend that average 0.5/0.5 with the existing XGBoost model.
Increase the Morgan fingerprint radius from 2 to 3 by changing the RADIUS setting, so each molecule's bit vector encodes a larger atom neighborhood.
Abort: add max_depth=5 and min_child_weight to the XGBoost component as a regularization tweak, which I judged not worth a slot given the prior depth-4 result (slot 12).
Add a LightGBMRegressor as a third member of the RF/XGB blend and combine the three predictions with equal 1/3 weights.
Lower the random forest's MAX_FEATURES from 0.3 to 0.2 so each split considers fewer features, adding tree diversity.
Set the XGBoost component's subsample to 0.7 and colsample_bytree to 0.7 (from 0.8 and 0.5) to add row and column subsampling regularization.
Change the Morgan fingerprint radius from 2 to 3 so the fingerprints capture larger local substructure contexts.
Lower the XGBoost component's learning rate from 0.05 to 0.01 and raise its tree count from 500 to 2500, a slower and smoother boosting path with the same total shrinkage (500 × 0.05 = 2500 × 0.01).

issues: None blocking. The only change is MIN_SAMPLES_LEAF going from 1 to 2 in the random forest. The diff has no file or network access, no pasted answers, no use of test labels and no bug.

Recomputed z: the candidate's loss of 0.5417 is 0.0016 worse than the incumbent's 0.5401. The standard error is 0.0070 × sqrt(1/1 + 1/2) ≈ 0.00857, so z ≈ -0.187. This matches the harness's -0.186; the small gap is likely from rounding.
Rejecting is correct. The candidate is slightly worse and well within noise, so the incumbent should stay.

description: Raise the random forest's MIN_SAMPLES_LEAF from 1 to 2 so each leaf needs at least two molecules, reducing overfitting on the 970-molecule set.
Replace the RandomForestRegressor with a LightGBM regressor (learning_rate=0.05, num_leaves=31, feature_fraction=0.8), keeping the 0.7/0.3 blend with XGBoost.
Set N_DESC to len(Descriptors.descList) so the featurizer uses every RDKit descriptor instead of the first 100, leaving the rest of train.py unchanged.
Drop the 20% lowest-variance features (fingerprint bits and descriptors, variance computed on the training fold only and applied to the test fold) before fitting the RF and XGBoost blend.
Standardize the training target (z-score using training-set mean and std, inverted on predictions) before fitting the RF/XGBoost blend.
Abort the Morgan radius 3 change because radius 3 was already tested in slot 23 and rejected (official 0.5492 vs incumbent 0.5159 under the current setup).
Skip: RobustScaler on the descriptor columns is a per-column monotone affine transform, which tree models (RF and XGBoost) are invariant to, so it should be a no-op.
Reduce the Morgan fingerprint size N_BITS from 2048 to 1024 to cut sparse-bit dimensionality and possibly improve generalization to unseen skeletons.

issues: No integrity problems found. The diff only adds L1 regularisation (reg_alpha=1.0) and L2 regularisation (reg_lambda=1.5) to the XGBoost part of the RF/XGB blend. It does not access files, paste in answers or use test labels, and it does not change the fit_predict signature or how the seed is used.
No bugs found. These are valid XGBRegressor parameters, and the rest of the pipeline is unchanged.

The candidate is 0.0044 worse than the incumbent (0.5203 vs 0.5159). That is well within the noise of a single run (sd 0.0070). Recomputing z as (0.5159 - 0.5203) / (0.0070 * sqrt(1/1 + 1/1)) gives about -0.44. This matches the harness value of -0.438 up to rounding, so rejecting the candidate is consistent.
Note: each side has only one run, so this comparison has very little statistical power. This small a change is unlikely to be worth a replicate slot.

description: Add L1 (reg_alpha=1.0) and L2 (reg_lambda=1.5) regularization to the XGBoost component of the RF/XGB blend.
Abort: swap XGBoost for LightGBM with an inner validation split for early stopping, which was judged not worth a slot.
Abort the z-score standardization of RDKit descriptors, since it is a per-column affine transform that leaves the tree-based RF and XGBoost models' splits unchanged.
Abort: raise the random forest and XGBoost tree counts to 1000 as a hyperparameter tweak, which is not worth a slot.

Abort: the proposed XGBoost max_depth=4 plus min_child_weight=3 regularization repeats a tested direction (depth 4 was rejected at 0.5444 in slot 12) and the regularization family has had no accepted edits.
Abort: changing the Morgan fingerprint radius from 2 to 3 duplicates slot 23, which was already tested and rejected (official 0.5492 vs incumbent 0.5159).
Skipped: z-scoring the RDKit descriptor columns is a per-column affine transform, which tree-based RF and XGBoost models are invariant to, so no change is expected.
Train the models on the reciprocal target 1/(y+1) when all training targets are positive, and invert predictions as 1/max(p, 1e-3) - 1, to emphasise differences at low clearance values.
Train three random forests with different seeds (seed, seed+1, seed+2) and average their predictions in place of the single random forest.
Add gamma=0.1 (minimum loss reduction to split) and reg_lambda=1.0 (L2 penalty) to the XGBRegressor component, using reg_lambda because lambda is a reserved Python keyword.

Add the 167-bit RDKit MACCS keys fingerprint (MACCSkeys.GenMACCSKeys) to the feature vector alongside the Morgan bits and all RDKit descriptors, and skip the Crippen fragment part because the existing all-descriptor set already contains the fr_* fragment counts.
